tactics.title: De-duplicate and upgrade the blog BlogPosting schema
tactics.description: app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx hand-writes its own BlogPosting (Organization author, no dateModified, no @id, keywords-as-string). Replace it with the superior articleSchema() builder, and set author to the real human Person @id for E-E-A-T on this YMYL content.
tactics.implementationNote: Delete the inline jsonLd object in the blog page; import articleSchema from lib/schema. Extend the builder/post frontmatter to carry a real authorSlug -> author:{'@id':`${url}/team/${slug}#person`} with publisher staying #organization, plus a true dateModified and a real 1200x630 image. Add a BreadcrumbList (Home>Blog>Post) to the same graph.

tactics.title: Add per-route canonical URLs on every layout
tactics.description: alternates.canonical is only set on root, /blog and /blog/[slug]. The [service] and [slug] dynamic layouts and most static layouts (services, team, about, contact, tools, faq, resources) set title/description but NO canonical, so Google has to guess. Add alternates.canonical to each.
tactics.implementationNote: metadataBase is already set in root layout, so canonical can be a relative path: e.g. in app/services/[service]/layout.tsx return alternates:{canonical:`/services/${serviceSlug}`}; in app/team/[slug]/layout.tsx canonical:`/team/${resolvedParams.slug}`. Do the same for /services, /team, /about, /contact, /faq, /tools/* layouts. Centralize the base in siteConfig (already there).

tactics.title: Add BreadcrumbList sitewide
tactics.description: Still a supported rich result and a clear hierarchy signal for crawlers and AI answer engines. breadcrumbSchema() already exists; just call it on every non-home route.
tactics.implementationNote: Define a tiny per-route items array (Home -> Section -> Page) in each layout and inject graph([breadcrumbSchema(items), ...]). Keep names matching the visible page H1/title.

tactics.title: Treat FAQPage as an AEO signal, not a Google rich result
tactics.description: Google fully removed FAQ rich results (May 2026; report + Rich Results Test support dropped June 2026). Implement faqSchema() ONLY on the genuine /faq page (and any truly Q&A page), purely to feed AI answer engines clean question-answer pairs. Do not sprinkle FAQPage on non-Q&A pages chasing a dropdown that no longer exists.
tactics.implementationNote: Inject from app/faq/layout.tsx. Each Question.name must be the full question and acceptedAnswer.text the full answer, matching visible on-page text exactly. Validate with validator.schema.org (not the soon-removed FAQ path of Rich Results Test). Keep answers factual and compliant for YMYL.

tactics.title: Populate sameAs and complete the NAP/entity trust signals
tactics.description: siteConfig.sameAs is intentionally empty. Confirm and add the real Google Business Profile, Facebook, LinkedIn (and X if any) URLs — sameAs is one of the strongest entity-disambiguation and E-E-A-T signals for both Google Knowledge Graph and AI citation, and is what ties your site to your Google reviews/local pack.
tactics.implementationNote: Add verified URLs to siteConfig.sameAs (organizationSchema already conditionally emits sameAs). Ensure the NAP (name/address/phone) in schema EXACTLY matches the Google Business Profile string-for-string. Also add per-person sameAs (LinkedIn) on team Person nodes. Never invent profiles.

tactics.title: Harden JSON-LD serialization against XSS
tactics.description: components/seo/JsonLd.tsx uses JSON.stringify(data) with dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Per official Next.js guidance, JSON.stringify does NOT escape '<', allowing potential script-breakout if any field ever contains user/CMS input (e.g. blog frontmatter, FAQ answers).
tactics.implementationNote: Change to JSON.stringify(data).replace(/</g,'\\u003c') in JsonLd.tsx (Next.js's documented mitigation), or adopt serialize-javascript. Low effort, removes a real injection vector as content becomes CMS-driven.

tactics.title: Add schema-dts typing to lib/schema.ts
tactics.description: Builders return Record<string,unknown>, so typos in property names (e.g. areaServed vs areasServed) won't be caught. The official Next.js docs recommend typing JSON-LD with schema-dts.
tactics.implementationNote: npm i -D schema-dts and type builders as WithContext<FinancialService>, Person, Service, BlogPosting, etc. Catches invalid/misspelled properties at build time. Optional but valuable as schema grows.

tactics.title: Per-route OpenGraph/Twitter images (and explicit canonical OG URLs)
tactics.description: There is one global app/opengraph-image.tsx (good, on-brand, factual) and no twitter-image. For a content/E-E-A-T play, generate route-specific OG images for blog posts (title + author + date) and optionally service/team pages, improving click-through from social and AI surfaces.
tactics.implementationNote: Add app/blog/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx using next/og ImageResponse + generateImageMetadata if needed, reading the post by slug to render the title/author. Next auto-emits the og:image and twitter:image tags. The global opengraph-image already cascades to routes without their own. Add a twitter-image.tsx (or rely on Next mapping OG to Twitter when card=summary_large_image). Keep <=8MB OG / <=5MB Twitter or the build fails.

tactics.title: Set hreflang/locale alternates for en-CA
tactics.description: Schema declares inLanguage en-CA and OpenGraph locale en_CA, html lang is 'en'. There is no alternates.languages (hreflang). For a single-language site this is minor, but tightening the locale signal helps Canadian targeting.
tactics.implementationNote: Set <html lang="en-CA"> in app/layout.tsx, and optionally alternates:{languages:{'en-CA':'/'}} in root metadata + x-default. Only add multiple hreflang entries if/when a fr-CA version exists — don't fabricate alternates.

tactics.title: Core Web Vitals discipline for the framer-motion + next/image stack
tactics.description: framer-motion (v11) ships meaningful client JS and above-the-fold animations can delay LCP and hurt INP — the metrics Google and the 2025 Web Almanac flag as hardest to pass. next.config.js already does optimizePackageImports for lucide-react and good image formats; extend the discipline.
tactics.implementationNote: 1) Give the LCP hero image priority + explicit width/height (reserve space -> CLS 0) and avoid animating it in. 2) Keep heavy framer-motion sections below the fold and lazy/viewport-gated; respect prefers-reduced-motion. 3) Convert 'use client' marketing pages (services/[service], team/[slug], faq) to server components where possible so content is in the initial HTML (better LCP + crawlability + lets JSON-LD live on the page) — these read static data and don't need useParams. 4) Add optimizePackageImports for framer-motion and recharts; lazy-load recharts/Chart tool pages with next/dynamic. 5) Self-host or preconnect fonts (already next/font with display swap). Measure with PageSpeed Insights field data, target LCP<2.5s, INP<200ms, CLS<0.1.

tactics.title: Strengthen YMYL E-E-A-T technical signals around authorship
tactics.description: For a 'Your Money' site, Google and AI answer engines weight author expertise and trust heavily. Tie every advice-bearing page to a real, credentialed human and a transparent firm.
tactics.implementationNote: Give blog posts a visible byline linking to /team/[slug] whose Person schema carries jobTitle, LLQP hasCredential, knowsAbout and sameAs. Add a 'reviewed by'/last-updated line on financial guidance pages (and reflect it in dateModified). Ensure About/Team pages state the LLQP licensing and registered-advisory status (no CFP/CFA). Add an Organization knowsAbout/areaServed that matches the real service set. These are the technical hooks Google AI Mode uses to verify claims and assess source credibility.

tactics.title: Tidy sitemap & robots accuracy
tactics.description: app/sitemap.ts sets lastModified:new Date() (today) on every static page each build, which dilutes the signal, and hardcodes the tool/service/team slug lists separately from siteConfig (drift risk). robots.ts is fine (allows all, disallows /admin /api, points to sitemap).
tactics.implementationNote: Drive sitemap entries from siteConfig.services/team and the blog index so lists never drift. Use real lastModified (git mtime or post.publishedAt/updatedAt) instead of new Date() for static pages so 'changed' actually means changed. Confirm the live sitemap is submitted in Google Search Console. priority/changeFrequency are weak hints — fine as-is.

area: Content Strategy — Topic Clusters & Blog Calendar
summary: Birchtree Financial has 8 existing blog posts (RRSP/TFSA/RESP limits, CPP/OAS, estate planning, investment, mortgage, tax-saving) but no pillar-and-cluster architecture, no local/Alberta angle, and no internal-linking spine connecting blog posts to its 6 services or 9 existing /tools/* calculators. The opportunity is to convert flat blog posts into 6 service-anchored topic clusters, add a 7th "Olds & Central Alberta" local pillar and an 8th "Farm, Ranch & Business-Owner Planning" pillar (justified by Olds/Sundre/Red Deer testimonial clients and the agricultural region), then layer a seasonal calendar (RRSP season Jan-Feb, tax season Mar-Apr, mid-year reviews, year-end Oct-Dec). Google's 2025 core updates reward topical depth and consistent internal linking; FAQ-structured, question-led content is 3.2x more likely to surface in AI Overviews, so every brief is written for both human readers and answer engines. Below are 8 pillar pages plus 18 net-new cluster/landing/tool/glossary briefs (26 total contentIdeas) that fill genuine gaps without duplicating existing posts. Every dollar figure is flagged VERIFY against current CRA because limits change annually and the firm must not publish stale numbers.

tactics.title: Build 8 pillar pages as the architecture spine (6 service + 2 strategic)
tactics.description: Create one long-form pillar page (2,000-3,500 words) per cluster: (1) Retirement Planning, (2) Investment Management, (3) Insurance Strategies, (4) Tax Optimization, (5) Wealth Building & Advisory, (6) Estate Planning Guidance — each living at or linked from the matching /services/[service] page — plus two strategic pillars: (7) 'Financial Planning in Olds & Central Alberta' (local hub) and (8) 'Farm, Ranch & Business-Owner Succession in Alberta'. Each pillar gives a broad overview and links DOWN to every cluster post; each cluster post links UP to its pillar with descriptive anchor text. This is the model Google's June 2025 core update rewards (topical authority, ~30% more organic traffic, rankings hold 2.5x longer than standalone posts).
tactics.implementationNote: In Next.js App Router, pillars can be static pages under /services/[service] (already exists) or dedicated routes like /financial-planning-olds-alberta. Reuse the existing MDX pipeline in content/blog for cluster posts. Add a typed 'pillar' and 'cluster' field to MDX frontmatter so you can auto-render 'Part of: [Pillar]' breadcrumbs and a cluster index on each pillar.

tactics.title: Map the existing 8 posts into clusters before writing anything new
tactics.description: Slot current posts under pillars so no work is wasted: understanding-rrsp-contribution-limits + cpp-oas-changes -> Retirement pillar; tfsa-contribution-limits + tax-saving-strategies -> Tax Optimization pillar; investment-strategies -> Investment pillar; estate-planning-essentials -> Estate pillar; resp-contribution-guide -> Wealth Building pillar; mortgage-planning -> Wealth Building pillar. Retrofit each with an up-link to its pillar and 2-3 sibling links. This instantly creates topical structure from content you already own.
tactics.implementationNote: Edit frontmatter + add a closing 'Related at Birchtree' link block to each of the 8 existing .mdx files. No new copy required beyond link sections.

tactics.title: Wire blog/cluster posts to the 9 existing /tools/* calculators and /contact
tactics.description: The site already has retirement-calculator, resp-planner, risk-profiler, tfsa-rrsp-analyzer, tax-optimization-calculator, cpp-oas-optimizer, savings-calculator, net-worth-tracker, bank-loan-calculator. Every relevant cluster post should embed a contextual CTA to the matching tool (e.g. RRSP post -> tfsa-rrsp-analyzer + retirement-calculator) and every tool result screen should link back to the explanatory pillar. This builds an internal-linking loop (content -> tool -> service -> contact) that lifts both rankings and conversions.
tactics.implementationNote: Create a reusable <ToolCTA tool='...' /> client component that renders a card linking to /tools/[tool]. Drop it into MDX via the existing MDX component map so editors can add it inline.

tactics.title: Make every post answer-engine ready (AEO) with a 40-60 word answer block + FAQPage schema
tactics.description: Open each post and pillar with a concise 40-60 word direct answer to the title question, use real questions as H2/H3 headings, and add 3-5 FAQs with FAQPage JSON-LD. Pages with FAQ schema are ~3.2x more likely to appear in Google AI Overviews and saw materially higher citation rates in ChatGPT/Perplexity in 2025. This is the single highest-leverage AEO move and pairs with the geo content to win 'financial advisor near me / in Olds' style queries.
tactics.implementationNote: The site has NO JSON-LD yet. Add Article + FAQPage + (for service pages) Service schema via Next.js by rendering a <script type='application/ld+json'> in each route. Build a small schema helper in /lib so the blog [slug] layout injects Article+FAQPage automatically from frontmatter.

tactics.title: Run the seasonal calendar so timely posts publish before peak search demand
tactics.description: Publish/refresh on the Canadian finance calendar: RRSP-season content live by early January (deadline ~late Feb/early March — VERIFY), tax-filing content by mid-February (filing deadline ~April 30 — VERIFY), FHSA/first-home content in spring, mid-year portfolio + insurance reviews in June-July, and year-end tax-loss-selling / TFSA-top-up / charitable-giving content in October-November. Refresh the contribution-limit posts every January when CRA confirms new numbers. One thoroughly-researched post per month outperforms weekly thin content.
tactics.implementationNote: Maintain an editorial calendar (even a simple JSON or CMS field) keyed to publishedAt. Set a recurring January task to update all dollar figures the moment CRA confirms limits, so the site is never the stale result.

tactics.title: Establish E-E-A-T and YMYL trust signals on every money page
tactics.description: Finance is YMYL (Your Money Your Life); Google and AI engines weight author expertise and trust heavily. Attribute every post to a named Birchtree advisor with a bio linking to their /team/[slug] page, state LLQP licensing and the fiduciary/fee-only positioning, add 'reviewed/updated' dates, and cite primary sources (CRA, Canada.ca) inline. Do NOT claim CFP/CFA or any designation the firm does not hold.
tactics.implementationNote: Add author + reviewedDate frontmatter fields; render an author card pulling from the existing /team data. Add Person/author to the Article JSON-LD.

tactics.title: Create a finance glossary hub to capture long-tail + definitional AI queries
tactics.description: A /glossary or /resources glossary of 30-50 Canadian finance terms (LCGE, FHSA, attribution rules, spousal RRSP, eligible vs non-eligible dividends, segregated funds, probate, RRIF) gives short, schema-friendly definition blocks that answer engines love to cite and that internally link to the relevant pillar/cluster. Each entry is a natural internal-linking anchor target.
tactics.implementationNote: Build one /glossary route rendering DefinedTerm JSON-LD per entry; cross-link each term to its parent pillar. Reuse the existing /resources/[slug] dynamic route pattern.

tactics.title: Differentiate from generic national content with a defensible local + niche moat

Keep community ties (Olds Grizzlys, 4-H, BGC Olds, MVESS) for an About/community page that reinforces local relevance, not as blog filler.

contentIdeas.whyItMatters: Anchor pillar for the Retirement service; links down to RRSP, CPP/OAS, RRIF, and decumulation cluster posts. Mention any CPP/OAS/RRSP dollar amounts only with VERIFY against current CRA. Reinforces LLQP/fiduciary positioning, no CFP/CFA claims.

Minimum-withdrawal percentages and age-71 conversion deadline are CRA-set: flag VERIFY against current CRA. Links up to Retirement pillar, across to cpp-oas-changes, and to /tools/retirement-calculator.

contentIdeas.title: How Much Do You Need to Retire in Alberta? A Realistic Framework
contentIdeas.whyItMatters: Local-intent retirement query with thin competition; ties Alberta cost-of-living to a planning framework. Keep any figures illustrative/general and flag VERIFY against current CRA for contribution-room references. Strong CTA to /tools/retirement-calculator and /contact.

contentIdeas.whyItMatters: Anchor pillar for the Investment service; absorbs existing investment-strategies post as a cluster. General education only (no securities/return promises). Links to /tools/risk-profiler and /tools/net-worth-tracker.

contentIdeas.title: TFSA vs RRSP: Which Should You Prioritize in 2026?
contentIdeas.whyItMatters: High-volume evergreen comparison the firm does not yet own as a head-to-head; complements (does not duplicate) the separate TFSA and RRSP limit posts. 2026 TFSA $7,000 / RRSP $33,810 figures cited only with VERIFY against current CRA. Links to /tools/tfsa-rrsp-analyzer.

contentIdeas.title: FHSA Explained: The First Home Savings Account for Canadian Buyers
contentIdeas.whyItMatters: Major gap — no FHSA content exists despite high search demand and relevance to younger Olds/central-Alberta families. $8,000/year, $40,000 lifetime limits flag VERIFY against current CRA. Links up to Wealth Building pillar and to /tools/savings-calculator.

contentIdeas.title: Understanding Investment Risk: How to Find Your Risk Tolerance
contentIdeas.whyItMatters: Definitional/AEO-friendly post that feeds the Investment pillar and routes readers directly into /tools/risk-profiler, tightening the content-to-tool-to-contact loop.

contentIdeas.title: Insurance Strategies for Canadian Families: Life, Critical Illness & Disability
contentIdeas.whyItMatters: Anchor pillar for the Insurance service and the firm's core LLQP-licensed competency (life + accident & sickness) — currently NO insurance blog content exists, a significant gap. Education only; no product/price guarantees. Links to Estate and Farm/Business pillars (key-person and buy-sell insurance).
